We just see what needs to be provided, what steps need to be taken. Can you tell us, do you know who is the author of this document; and when and where it was drawn up?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm fully familiar with this document. The author of this aide-memoire, or checklist, for instructive inspection is myself, personally. We used certain parts of this checklist when conducting instructive visits also. As I have said earlier, crime prevention administration, with its headquarters at the ministry, had problems with human resources. I'm here referring to the fact that we were forced to hire crime police workers for our administration who had experience in crime prevention matters but only at the municipal level; at the level of municipal organs. And none of them ever held a position in the former Ministry of the Interior of the former Bosnia and Herzegovina, nor have experience of working in the headquarters of the ministry or in the crime police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What you just told us, was that the reason why you drew up this checklist or not; and could you tell us when this checklist was written, approximately?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the reason for me to write this checklist, or aide-memoire. And another reason was the quality of the reports they wrote following instructive visits. The checklist was written either in December 1992 or in January 1993. I wrote it personally. I consulted my colleagues to make sure that I covered everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me show you another document. I think we have sufficient time before the break. That's 65 ter 50D1, tab 99. Mr. Macar, earlier on we spoke about the situation at the Pale SJB and about the removal of Mr. Malko Koroman, the chief of the SJB, the attempt to remove him in early 1992 and also his subsequent removal in 1993, in early 1993. We see here a report dated March 1993. This is a report on the inspection and activities of the Pale SJB and the activities of its crime investigation service for the period from April to December 1992. It says at the bottom that the report was written by Minic, Ostoja. This is page 6 of this document. Tell me please, do you know this report? And to which administration did Inspector Ostoja Minic belong?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with this report. And as for Mr. Minic, he worked for the crime police administration in the ministry headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether this was the first inspection of the Pale SJB after the MUP of Republika Srpska was established?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was the first inspection done by a member of the crime police administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 5 of this document, in the Serbian text, there is a proposal of measures and action. And then there's three paragraphs, 1, 2, and 3. That's almost at the end of the document. Page 5 and 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see now that there is a mistake in the translation of this document. The original says that the report is for the period April-December 1992. Whereas, on the first page of the translation, it says April to December 1993. Since the report was written in March of 1993, it is obvious that this is a mistake in translation, and we will resolve it with the translation service.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, very briefly, can you give us a brief comment of these proposed measures and activities that your inspector, Ostoja Minic, gave following the inspection and visit of the SJB?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The proposed measures and activities were a result of the anomalies that he recorded in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In item 3, he emphasises the will and initiative displayed by the newly appointed chief of the SJB, Pekic, Petko, to deal with the accumulated problems: "So far, we have had full co-operation and we expect it to be so in the future." Do you remember whether Petko Pekic was appointed as chief of the SJB following the removal of Malko Koroman?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This report, which pertains to the 1992, did you see it in early 1993, once your inspector wrote it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately after it was written, I received the report, and I discussed it with Mr. Minic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D644, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see the time, Your Honour. Time for the break? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... we return in 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please continue, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I was asked by Mr. Hannis at the beginning of today's session for couple of minutes -- that we adjourn a couple of minutes before, because this is an housekeeping matter, as I understood, to be discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did want to raise something concerning an agreement about adjudicated facts. It's long standing, and it's just a matter of trying to get something on the record. But I think actually maybe it is better if I do it tomorrow or Monday when I'm more organised and have all the background information. So I encourage my friend to use the full time remaining.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you very much. [Interpretation] Could we please see document 108D1, tab 103.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document dated 21 May 1993 and it refers to the dispatch of -- from the CSB Banja Luka, dated 20 May 1993, the entire contents of which is quoted. And in the signature block we read: "Chief of the public security station, Bogdan Delic." And as far as I can tell, it was forwarded to the Kozarac police station. We read in paragraph 2: "Due to poor communication within the OUP and the lack of resourcefulness of some individuals in leading positions, neither the Security Services Centre nor the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska have been kept regularly informed of these events." It also says further down: "Deliver detailed information on all disturbances of law and order, criminal offences committed in your area in the period from 4 April to 31 December 1992 and 1 January to 15 May 1993." It goes on to say: "The report should include all these events and contain a precise description of the place and time, the offence and its consequences, as well as the measures taken by the OUP or the military security organ." A deadline was set, and the original CSB dispatch was signed by Stojan Zupljanin. Do you know who Bogdan Delic is?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I think he was a mathematics teacher. He hailed from Sokolac. I met him in Prijedor and he was appointed station chief, after Mr. Drljaca was removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The situation described in this document, were you familiar with it in 1993 when this was drafted?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If I may say briefly, that, as a consequence of the relocation of the MUP to Bijeljina, apart from the organisation of the lines of work, one of the priority tasks was the setting up of an information system from the stations --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. Could you repeat the last sentence because you hurried again so it wasn't recorded: "One of the priority tasks was the setting up of an information system from the stations," and the rest is missing.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Setting up a system of passing on information about security-relevant events along the following line: SJB, CSB, administrations at headquarters, or Ministry of the Interior, and vice versa, to make possible information flow from the ministry, or the administrations at our headquarters through the CSBs down to the SJBs. Because the system of passing on information had almost completely stopped functioning so that the leadership in many cases was not informed of the events on the ground. After visiting the centres, we observed that the CSBs were not regularly informed by the SJBs, nor were they informed in a timely fashion. And if I may add, this request was sent out because in 1993 the technical equipment and the communication technology was much better and could make possible better information flow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said that the leadership in many cases was not informed of the events on the ground. Which leadership did you mean? Leadership of what?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The administrations at headquarters were not informed, the head of the public security department or -- and the minister, and we also observed that the SJBs did not pass on information along the lines of work to the responsible person at the centre. And then, of course, the centre chief also did not receive that information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, do you know of the crime committed at Koricanske Stijene in August 1992? When did you learn of it?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: In August 1992, I was unaware of the incident at Koricanske Stijene, or whatever the place is called. As far as I remember, in late 1992 or early 1993 I got the first information. When I was visiting the centre with the team, that's when I first heard of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you were visiting the centre with your team, did you then get complete information about the crimes committed at Koricanske Stijene?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The head of the crime police --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please answer first with a yes or a no. I asked you this because part of your answer, unfortunately, again, didn't make it to the transcript. Please answer yes or no.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us when it was and what you were told then. What did the head of the crime police at the Banja Luka CSB say to you then?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was March 1993. He informed me of the event at Koricanske Stijene, saying that about 150 - I'm not speaking from memory -- 150 Serbs [as interpreted] had been killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said Serbs?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said non-Serbs. Once they got that information with the public prosecutor's office from Banja Luka, and the military prosecutor's office, military magistrate, security organs -- military organs, that is, they began an on-site investigation led by two prosecutors. On the team of the CSB, there were violent crime inspectors and forensic technicians from the crime enforcement service of the Banja Luka centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed about any criminal complaints filed?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed that a criminal complaint against unknown perpetrators was filed with the prosecutor's office that had jurisdiction there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Were -- were you informed of the results of the efforts to identify the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed that two or three perpetrators had been identified, and that, according to the information the security centre had gathered, those persons were members of the reserve force or some other police unit from Prijedor, that they had left the Prijedor area and allegedly joined the army, some army unit. According to the information they gave me, the CSB took measures to try and locate these persons through the corps police, in order to take them in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "corps police," what do you mean? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the security organs of the Krajina Corps. I cannot remember which unit it exactly was, but it was the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, are you moving on to something else because I have a question relating to this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour. I had another question, but, please, by all means.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Macar, that's something that confuses me a bit in this document that we have on the screen, because the instruction from the chief of the SJB in Prijedor starts out by saying that since the outbreak of the war, there have been breaches of law and order, criminal offences and conflicts of all kinds between employees of the OUP internal affairs organ, and the members of the VRS army. And then two paragraphs further down, he is then asking the Kozarac police station to provide information on all disturbances of law and order or criminal offences committed in your area by members of the Army of Republika Srpska in a certain period. What confuses me is that I thought that the power to investigate the crimes committed by the members of the VRS would fall under the authority of the military police and that all activities or crimes would be investigated and perhaps prosecuted by the military prosecutor. Whereas, here, it seems as if the civilian police is now suddenly called upon to investigate crimes committed by the members of the army. So my question to you is: Does this letter or this instruction represent a transgression of the civilian police's authority into the authority of the military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For criminal offences committed by VRS members, the authority was with the military security organs and military judiciary organs. In case of an attack of the military police on the civilian police, the latter would certainly ask its members about the event and submit the relevant information to the military police or the military judicial organs. As has been said already, the setting up of military judicial organs only began sometime in summer 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: But you haven't answered my question about why it is that the civilian police is engaging itself in the investigations against members of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It wasn't possible to understand if the -- it was understandable if the military police did not respond to the reported event that the police of the RS would gather certain information and submit it. The RS police had no power to detain or arrest military personnel. They could hold them until the military police arrived and then hand over to the military police any material available to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: So do I understand correctly that this dispatch to the SJB in Kozarac was meant only to assist the military police in their investigations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This dispatch primarily requests that the Security Services Centre, through the ministry, should be informed about any security-related events in the territory covered by the Prijedor SJB.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand this fully. But maybe you should just proceed, Mr. Zecevic. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I will try to -- first, I have a correction in the transcript. But perhaps I should ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, your last answer, you say: "This dispatch primarily requests that the Security Services Centre, through the ministry, should be informed about any security-related events in the territory covered by the Prijedor SJB." I would say that there has been some permutation there. Can you please slowly repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's obviously been a mistake. My answer was this: The instructions from dispatch ordered that the SJB in Prijedor inform about any security-related events, the public security centre, through which the Ministry of the Interior at the HQ would be informed. If I may quote the dispatch: "Because of the insufficient linkage between the organs of the Ministry of the Interior or the failure of certain employees to find their feet, the public security centre, or, indeed, the Ministry of the Interior of the RS were not informed about these events in a timely manner."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, does this memo simply seek information or are other activities proposed here?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not just about information regarding the actual events. It's also information about measures taken by organs of the Ministry of the Interior, as well as military security organs, related to specific events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does this document make any reference to an order to conduct an investigation in relation to certain events?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last part of the document focuses on the fact that --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, just a minute, please. My question is very clear: Does this memo simply seek information or does it contain an order to conduct an investigation?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order seeks information so that one would be able to take in the security-related situation over the preceding period about which we had not been informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that everything that they say in this document?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours? [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to tender this document for admission. It's in relation to 1992, although it was produced in 1993, which I believe constitutes its relevance to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure what the relevance is. They want reporting about conflicts between the army and the MUP, as I read this document. We already have evidence about that, the fact that there may not have been sufficient reporting about it, I'm not sure how it adds to our case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me respectfully read again this document: "There have been breaches of law and order, criminal offences and conflicts of all kinds ..." Therefore, it refers to the breaches of law and order, criminal offences and the conflicts. And the relevance of this document is that it refers to the situation in -- from 4th April until 31st December 1992 and also is indicative of the fact that Mr. Simo Drljaca has been removed from his position by at least May 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, it indicates someone else is in the position of chief as of May 1993. But it doesn't indicate that Mr. Drljaca has been removed or punished or sanctioned. It may indicated that he has been promoted or moved to a higher position. As for this document, paragraph 3 says: In order to gain an insight into these events, make a competent assessment of relations between the OUP, the police, and the VRS. Deliver to us information about disturbances in law and order or criminal offences committed in your area by members of the army. So it is about the relation between the army and the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 1D645, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Macar, are you familiar with a paramilitary formation known as Yellow Wasps?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember whether the Ministry of the Interior carried out an action against this group? If you do remember, if you're aware of it, could you perhaps tell us what specifically was done during that action.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Ministry of the Interior, in co-operation with members of the VRS, took activities to disarm and bring in the paramilitary unit known as Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Our next document is 1D75, tab 49. Did the crime prevention administration have any role to play in this action; and, if so, what role, specifically?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime police administration used some of its men to assist the Bijeljina public security station as they were trying to shed light on certain general crimes that occurred. The crimes were perpetrated by members of the paramilitary formation known as the Yellow Wasps.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, the memo is dated the 4th of August, 1992. It talks about the activities taken by the MUP to shed light on the criminal activities of a paramilitary formation in the territory of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik. The memo, or report, was not signed. Nevertheless, we've had a chance to see a cover letter that was attached to this memo, bearing the same date that was submitted to the ministry, the HQ. Are you familiar with this report or memo?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was this memo produced by your own crime prevention administration or was it produced by one of the employees?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was produced by the employees of the crime prevention administration, and, in part, also by people from the Bijeljina public security station who took part in this procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your comment, please, on the last paragraph of this document, which is page 3. It talks about information obtained by the Serb armed forces military police and MUP national security operatives, indicating that Dusan Vuckovic, also known as Repic, was committing a massacre-genocide over citizens of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina of Muslim ethnicity. It goes on to state: "Verification and materialisation of these -- of this information was being performed by the Serb armed forces military police in co-operation with the MUP national security operatives." Is this a faithful reflection of the information that was available to you at the time in relation to the actions of this man known as Repic and what he did to these ethnic Muslims, who were also citizens of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say briefly the following: Information on the war crimes committed by Dusan Vuckovic was available to both the public security stations and to the national security. All this information was forwarded to the military police and then pressed the matter further with the military prosecutor. They took some operative steps to process this information, and probably also information that was available to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say process this information, would that also include pressing charges for these crimes against the perpetrators?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what I had in mind. It is up to the military police to file a report to the prosecutor, and then the prosecutor makes a request for an investigation to take place and then the indictment follows.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What about the crime prevention administration of the MUP of the RS? Did it also submit criminal reports against members of this same paramilitary unit; and, if so, do you remember which?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. The public security station to which it was to file criminal reports processed many cases of property-related crimes. It filed a criminal report to the relevant prosecutor in Bijeljina. If I may just say one thing that I believe is noteworthy. Having reached agreement with the military police and the military prosecutor, or, rather, involved in reaching agreement with those bodies were Mr. Davidovic and Mr. Andan, who were directly involved in the action. They assumed the responsibility to elucidate some of the property related -- to have this elucidated by the Ministry of the Interior and the public security station in Bijeljina which we were helping at the time. So they were supposed to elucidate some of these property-related crimes perpetrated by members of this military unit, paramilitary unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope the transcript will be adjusted and corrected, because at this point in time, I'm unable to ascertain whether what the witness said was, in fact, recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just slowly, please, proceed with telling us your answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Davidovic and Mr. Andan explained to me that, following a suggestion that was made by a member of the military police, they accepted that the Ministry of the Interior should investigate some of these property-related crimes, because there was information that was in the possession of several different public security stations regarding individual crimes. When I say in several different stations, citizens who sustained damage as a result of these crimes, somewhere along the Sarajevo-Zvornik road had goods on items seized or taken from them as they were travelling. Since this was in a forest somewhere having returned to their places of residence, they would report these crimes. This part of such operative material, as had been gathered, was processed. We managed to identify several different crimes so the report or the criminal report was submitted to the relevant prosecutor in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm looking at this document in front of us and it is dated 4 August 1992. I see that it is stated here that members of this unit massacred and committed the crime of genocide against citizens of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina who were of Muslim ethnicity. So you had information that they had committed a war crime. Why did not the crime enforcement service of the MUP of Republika Srpska initiate criminal proceedings against these persons for war crimes against the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Launching proceedings for crimes committed by the Yellow Wasps was under the jurisdiction of military bodies, the military prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the military bodies, that is, the military judiciary, ever initiated criminal proceedings against these persons for war crimes?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received informal or unofficial information that all legal measures had been taken. But they were not obliged to inform us in writing, so that I cannot confirm with full certainty what the final result of their efforts was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Such a division of labour, was it agreed upon with the military security organs? Namely, that they should be in charge of war crimes, and you in charge of crimes against property.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon the request of military security organs, Mr. Davidovic and Andan and the others who took part, accepted that they should deal with crimes against property. If I had been present personally, I would have insisted that if the military security organs needed assistance, that we should provide it --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please repeat your answer, because it was unclear to the interpreters. You said: "If I had been present personally, I would have insisted ...," but you didn't explain what you would have insisted on. Please try to be clearer in your answer.

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I had attended the meeting with the representatives of military security bodies, when there was discussion about the following division of labour. That some work but the resolving of crimes against property be taken by the civilian police, and that we could also --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter hasn't understood the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Once more, you were not understood, but possibly it will be clearer when I ask my following question: In your opinion, sir, why did the military judiciary have jurisdiction over the Yellow Wasps, rather than the civilian judiciary?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Yellow Wasps were members of the VRS, but they were not under the control of the VRS. They had broken loose.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document 65 ter of the Prosecution, or, actually, the Defence 964D1, which is tab 52.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the federal Ministry of the Interior. The date is 8 August 1992. It was handed to the minister personally. And it says: "Report on the engagement of a group of federal Ministry of the Interior police brigade members to provide expert assistance to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina MUP." On page 9, we see the signature of Milorad Davidovic. Tell me, first, if you remember who the federal minister of the interior was at the time?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was Mr. Gracanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said Mr. Gracanin?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me about Mr. Milorad Davidovic. Which ministry did he belong to?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information I had, until the war broke out, Mr. Davidovic was with the federal Ministry of the Interior of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You told us that Mr. Davidovic took part in the arrest of the Yellow Wasps. Does this apply to this Mr. Milorad Davidovic?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the preamble of this document, we read: "Due to the growing security problems in the area of north-eastern Bosnia which came to the fore in May and June, the MUP of the Serbian Republic of BH asked the federal secretary of the interior of the FRY to send, if possible, a number of police officers [sic] and brigade Deputy Commander of the SSUP, Milorad Davidovic, to this area with the aim of becoming directly engaged in stabilising the security situation, establishing the legality of work and normal functioning of the organs of internal affairs and ensuring the legitimacy of the authorities. The federal secretary accepted the request from -- of the SR BH MUP and sent a group of 17 members of the SSUP unit with the necessary weapons and three all-terrain vehicles to the Bijeljina CSB ... on 27 June 1992." Are you familiar with these facts; and can you confirm them, sir?

utterances.speaker: GORAN MACAR [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am; and I can confirm. Immediately before being deployed to Bijeljina, I believe that Mr. Davidovic was at Vrace to see Minister Stanisic. A day, or, anyway, a short time ago, he set off for Bijeljina where the unit was going to take care of the disrupted security situation, some clashes with military units, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would seek to tender this document. But the situation is as follows --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was only received by us very recently, and we wanted to include it on our 65 ter list which was not opposed by Mr. Hannis, so it was done. Had we been in the possession of this document earlier, we would have asked the gentleman who signed it to authenticate it. But since both the OTP and we received it only much later, I'm now in the position to have to seek its admission through this witness, and I believe it is not in dispute that it is highly relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to say this is a document the Prosecution has been looking for for years. Mr. Davidovic testified about it when he testifying in the Krajisnik case. But he explained that his copy of this document was taken when his apartment was searched many years ago in Belgrade. It was produced by Mr. Karadzic during Mr. Karadzic's trial when he was examining Mr. Davidovic. I think that was the 26th or 27th of June. When we received it, we turned it over to the Defence. We would have liked to have had it when he was here. But Mr. Davidovic confirmed in the Karadzic case - I can get you the citation if you need it - that this, indeed, is a report that he authored and sent to his boss in the federal SUP back in 1992. So I have no doubts about its authenticity nor its relevance, and I join in the request that it be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So it's admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D645, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can we check the number? I think we're up to 646 now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise. The counsel is correct. It's 1D646. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I note the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Macar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we take the adjournment now to reconvene tomorrow morning at 9.00. And I believe we're still in this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 8th day of July, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.46 p.m.,
